entities.summary: Giacomo Gastaldi was an Italian cartographer, astronomer and engineer of the 16th century, born in Venice around 1510, and died in Rome on October 24, 1566. As a prominent figure in the Renaissance era, he made significant contributions to the field of cartography, creating detailed maps of the Italian peninsula and the Mediterranean region. His work, 'La Carta dell' Italia', is considered one of the most accurate and influential maps of its time. Gastaldi's cartographic skills were also utilized by the Catholic Church, which employed him to create maps for the Index Librorum Prohibitorum. He also developed a system for measuring the size of the Earth, and his work on this topic was widely recognized during his lifetime. Gastaldi's legacy can be seen in the work of later cartographers, such as Ortelius, who built upon his discoveries. Through his contributions to cartography, Gastaldi played a role in shaping our understanding of the world during the Renaissance.
